rule: A worker target is advertised (SUPPORTED_TARGETS in packages/worker-bootstrap/src/manifest.ts) only when its row here is verified: the native lane ran green on a real host of that OS and architecture. tests/unit/native-support-matrix_test.ts enforces it.

rows.proof: Rendered systemd unit run in a disposable systemd container on an x86_64 host: install, pair, 0600 secrets, kill, restart, freeze/thaw, upgrade, canceled download, reboot, stop. The unit starts a shell stand-in for the worker, so this proves install, pairing and the service lifecycle on this architecture, not the worker program itself.

Same native file, run green on agx64 (aarch64, cgroup v2) on 2026-11-22. The unit starts a shell stand-in for the worker, so this proves install, pairing and the service lifecycle on this architecture, not the worker program itself.
Needs a real Mac runner (owner hardware): LaunchAgent load, supervisor and keychain secret boundary.
Needs a real Intel Mac runner (owner hardware).
Sleep is modelled with the cgroup freezer (systemctl freeze/thaw); a real host suspend and resume needs owner hardware.
Mac supervisor and keychain boundary need a Mac.
AC2 claim rule: a job whose requirements.platform is macos is never claimed by a Linux host with free capacity; it stays queued with no attempt until a macOS host claims it.
Mac build evidence (a real iOS job built with Xcode on a Mac worker) needs a Mac (owner hardware).
Chromium virtual authenticator: replay, wrong origin and RP ID, cancel and TOTP step-up; API-level replay and origin rejection.
Safari and iOS passkeys need Apple hardware.
A physical FIDO key needs a person at the machine.
